title: Microsoft Edge: share tenant-approved work browsing history with Microsoft 365 Copilot Search
summary: The briefing passes: the roadmap facts, default sharing behaviour, licence requirement and Edge policy controls are supported. Its documentation gaps are appropriately narrow; the sources checked do not explain how tenant-approved sites are selected for this particular sharing policy.

claims.where: title; summary; What's changing; Why it matters; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Edge can now send work-related browsing history to Microsoft 365 Copilot Search.
claims.quote: With admin approval, Microsoft Edge can now send selected work-related browsing history from third-party apps to Microsoft 365 Copilot to improve search result ranking.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Data exposure; Governance guidance; rationale: impact
claims.claim: Copilot Search can surface relevant recently visited work pages from browsing history.
claims.quote: When a user searches on Microsoft 365 Copilot Search, M365 Copilot will also surface results from work browsing history when relevant, helping users find recently visited work pages faster.

claims.claim: The roadmap describes the history as IT admin selected work related browsing history.
claims.quote: Microsoft Edge can now send IT admin selected work related browsing history to Copilot to improve search relevance.

claims.quote: Microsoft Edge can now send selected work-related browsing history from third-party apps to Microsoft 365 Copilot

claims.claim: The release notes describe this sharing as occurring with admin approval.

claims.claim: Sharing is on by default for eligible users when the policy is enabled or not configured.
claims.quote: If you enable or don't configure this policy, browsing history will be shared with Microsoft 365 Copilot Search by default, and users can turn off sharing using the toggle in Microsoft Edge settings.

claims.where: What's changing; Why it matters; Risk assessment; controls[0].note; Governance controls
claims.claim: Users can turn sharing off with a toggle in Edge settings while the policy is enabled or unconfigured.
claims.quote: If you enable or don't configure this policy, browsing history will be shared with Microsoft 365 Copilot Search by default, and users can turn off sharing using the toggle in Microsoft Edge settings.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment; Governance guidance; controls[0].governs; Governance controls
claims.claim: Disabling ShareBrowsingHistoryWithCopilotSearchAllowed stops sharing history with Copilot Search.
claims.quote: If you disable this policy, browsing history won't be shared with Microsoft 365 Copilot Search.

claims.claim: The feature requires the user to be signed in to Edge with an Entra ID account.

claims.where: controls[1].ui and api; Why it matters; Risk assessment; Governance guidance; Open questions
claims.claim: Microsoft Learn does not document the admin UI or API that selects tenant-approved sites for this Edge history-sharing policy.
claims.quote: Searched: '"ShareBrowsingHistoryWithCopilotSearchAllowed" "sites" "approve"' and Edge tenant approved sites configure connector activity settings; read sharing policy, extension page and approved-domains excerpts. No passage links a selection control to this sharing policy.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Open questions
claims.claim: The sharing-policy page does not describe where shared browsing history is stored.
claims.quote: Searched: 'Edge browsing history Copilot Search eligible licenses pricing meter retention delete data consent'; read the complete sharing-policy page and Edge privacy and Copilot privacy excerpts. The policy page states no storage location.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Open questions
claims.claim: The sharing-policy page does not describe how long shared browsing history is retained.
claims.quote: Searched: 'Edge browsing history Copilot Search eligible licenses pricing meter retention delete data consent'; read the complete sharing-policy page and Edge privacy and Copilot privacy excerpts. The policy page specifies no retention period.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Open questions
claims.claim: The sharing-policy page does not describe whether shared browsing history can be deleted.
claims.quote: Searched: 'Edge browsing history Copilot Search eligible licenses pricing meter retention delete data consent'; read the complete sharing-policy page and Edge privacy and Copilot privacy excerpts. The policy page gives no deletion procedure.

claims.where: Cost and licensing: Meter; rationale: cost
claims.claim: The sharing-policy page and release notes describe no meter or charge for this feature.
claims.quote: Searched: '"Edge" "Copilot Search" "browsing history" "meter" "charge"'; read sharing policy and both release-note feature entries, plus Search licensing excerpts. No feature-specific meter or charge is stated in the policy or release notes.

claims.claim: The cited sources do not describe this history-sharing feature taking actions.
claims.quote: Searched: '"Edge" "Copilot Search" "browsing history" "actions"'; read sharing policy, both release-note entries and connector extension page. They describe sharing history and ranking search results, not autonomous actions by this feature.

claims.claim: The Microsoft 365 Copilot extension captures activity from administrator-approved applications.
claims.quote: The extension collects signals only from administrator-approved applications and doesn't track general web browsing.

claims.claim: The browser extension uses connector activity settings to map visited URLs to indexed items.
claims.quote: To enable activity signals, you must configure activity settings on the connector so the system can map visited URLs to indexed item IDs.

claims.claim: The extension page does not state that its connector activity settings select sites shared by Edge under ShareBrowsingHistoryWithCopilotSearchAllowed.
claims.quote: Searched: 'Edge ShareBrowsingHistoryWithCopilotSearchAllowed tenant approved sites configure administrator approval connector activity settings'; read the full extension and sharing-policy pages. The extension page describes the installed extension, not this built-in sharing policy.
